newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Prairie harvest 2 weeks from finish-Pioneer.
newsitem.headline: Canada Prairie harvest 2 weeks from finish-Pioneer.

text.p: Canada's Prairie harvest was expected to be complete in the next week or two except for the extreme northwest where some crops may not be combined until spring, Pioneer Grain Co Ltd said in a report for the week ended Oct 16.

Harvest in British Columbia's Dawson Creek region and Alberta's Peace River Valley advanced to 20 percent complete by Sunday from 15 percent a week earlier. Snow in the north on Wednesday delayed harvest. Some farmers believe 50 percent of the crop will have to be harvested in the spring.
Alberta's harvest was 60 percent complete with another 10 days needed to finish combining. Cold, wet weather caused sprouting in wheat and barley which will downgrade them.

Northwest Saskatchewan needs one more week to finish combining with 85 percent of canola, 75 percent of barley, 65 percent of wheat, 55 percent of oats, 40 percent of durum and 30 percent of flax harvested.

North central Saskatchewan needs one week to finish after harvest was stalled for the previous two weeks. About 75 percent of wheat, canola, 70 percent barley, 65 percent oats, 40 percent of durum and 25 percent of flax were in the bin.

Northeast Saskatchewan harvested 80 percent of wheat and oats, 50 percent of barley and canola and 25 percent of flax. The balance of the crop remaining to harvest will grade as Number Three or Feed grade.
Southwest Saskatchewan harvested 90 to 95 percent of its crops with flax lagging behind at 80 percent. Crop quality deteriorated on wet weather.

Southeast Saskatchewan harvested 85 percent of wheat, durum and oats while 90 percent of barley and canola were combined and 70 percent of flax was in the bin. Combining could be wrapped up with one week of good weather.
The cool, wet fall caused quality problems and it appeared 50 percent of wheat would grade Number One.
Eastern Saskatchewan and Manitoba harvests were near complete with one more week of good weather needed to finish combining. Crop quality appeared average.
